**Claim:** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat) — branch `claude/issue-6293-conditionbuilder-reference-quoting`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` in the same label write.

## Pre-dispatch gate

**1. Thread read.** Triage direction (18:09:14Z) read in full and adopted. It draws the scope line this dispatch enforces below.

**2. Shadow check.** Nothing in flight touches `packages/app-shell/`. ⚠️ **`#6296` is the Feature sibling** on this same component ("caller-supplied subject vocabulary: scope prefix + `previous`"). It is **not** dispatched and is **not** yours — see the boundary below.

**3. Premise live @ `origin/main`:** `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ConditionBuilder.tsx:56  function fmtValue(v: string): string`.

## Scope — the REPAIR, not the feature

`fmtValue` wraps anything that is not a number / `true` / `false` / `null` in quotes, **including a value that is plainly a reference**. An author building "this field differs from its prior value" gets `previous == 'previous.status'` — syntactically valid CEL, parses, registers, evaluates, and is **always false**. Nothing objects at any layer: `previous` is a declared root, and a string literal's contents are deliberately not scanned by `flow-ref-check` or by the server-side validator.

Live today at **all five** existing `ConditionBuilder` consumers, on the idiom that *defines* change-detection predicates.

The ruled scope: an input matching a declared root prefix (`record.`, `previous.`, and whatever roots the mounting surface declares) either

- **compiles as the reference it plainly is**, or
- **is refused loudly at commit** with a message naming both readings — e.g. "compare to the field `previous.status`, or to the literal text `'previous.status'`?"

⭐ **Refusal is acceptable; silence is not.** That is the whole card.

**You choose which of the two**, and the choice is a measurement, not a preference: **measure it against all five consumers** and report what you found. Compiling the reference is the better outcome where it is safe; if any consumer would break, refusing is the ruled fallback. Put the five readings in the PR body — one line per consumer, naming the consumer.

## ⛔ Out of scope — file, do not build

- **`#6296`** — the first-class "another field" value control (a proper reference picker) is a **Feature** and is explicitly beyond this card. ⛔ Do not implement it, do not partially implement it. If your repair makes it easier, say so in the report; the PM routes it.
- ⛔ Do not change what any predicate *means* elsewhere, do not touch `flow-ref-check` or the server-side expression validator, and do not touch `packages/spec`.
- The flow designer is where this was found, **not** where it lives. The defect is in `ConditionBuilder` itself. ⛔ Do not scope the fix to flow-entry surfaces only.

## Tests

Pin the **emitted CEL** — that is the observable, not the UI state:
- the **reference** case (`previous.status` typed into the value box) → whichever behaviour you ruled, asserted exactly;
- the **literal control** (`done`) → still `previous == 'done'`;
- the **number control** (`42`) → still `previous == 42`, unquoted. The card included this one specifically to show the quoting is value-dependent rather than unconditional — keep it, it is what makes the reading attributable to the input.
- ⛔ **Ghost-assertion guard (mandatory):** run each new assertion against unmodified `origin/main` first, capture it **failing**, then capture it passing. Both readings in the PR body.
- The card measured this by mounting the **real component** in jsdom and reading what `onCommit` emitted. Do the same — ⛔ do not unit-test `fmtValue` in isolation and call the surface covered: the commit path above it is part of the defect.

## Ground rules

Worktree-first: `git worktree add ../objectui-6293 -b claude/issue-6293-conditionbuilder-reference-quoting main && cd ../objectui-6293 && pnpm install`. ⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack lives in the common `.git` dir and is shared across every worktree of this repo; a `pop` silently restores another agent's work and reports success. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Changeset: `patch`, `@object-ui/app-shell`. Run the repo's fast checks before pushing. Open the PR as **draft** with `Fixes #6293` and report back — the PM lands it, ⛔ never self-merge.

Size: M. Model: opus.

**ACCEPT (pending green CI).** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`, `domain:ui` execution seat. Reviewed against the **tree**, not the report.

**Ruled arm: 1 — compile the reference.** The dispatch order left the choice to measurement; the dev measured all five consumers and found none that breaks, with a one-line reading per consumer in the PR body. That is the ruled procedure carried out, not a preference.

## ⭐ The judgment that makes this fix correct rather than merely working

**The trigger is not "contains a dot."** `REFERENCE_ROOTS` is scoped to the roots *this builder's own vocabulary already commits to* — `record` / `user` / `org` (its subject dropdown), `previous` / `parent` (bound by `evalFieldPredicate` and the server-side evaluators), `current_user` (the ADR-0068 alias). And it **deliberately excludes** `data`, `os`, `app`, `features`, `input`, `vars`, `page`, with the reason recorded in the source rather than only in the PR:

> `data.csv` is a plausible literal, and `data` IS bound, so reading it as a reference would produce another silently-false predicate instead of a loud one.

⭐ **A fix for a silent failure must not mint a new silent failure in the other direction.** Over-capturing here would have swapped `previous == 'previous.status'` (always false) for `data == data.csv` (always false, different cause) and called it progress. Verified anchored and dotted-identifier-only against the tree: `1.2.3`, filenames, and paths under unbound roots all stay literal.

## ⭐ The invariant I did not ask for, and should have

> **Nothing already stored is rewritten.** A persisted `previous == 'previous.status'` no longer round-trips, so the component's existing safety rule hands it to the raw CEL editor instead of reinterpreting it.

Traced through the tree: `unfmtValue` strips the quotes to `previous.status`, `fmtValue` now re-emits it **bare**, the two disagree, and the existing round-trip guard falls back rather than committing.

That matters more than it looks. Without it, merely *opening* an existing condition in the builder would silently flip a stored predicate from always-false to actually-comparing. That may well be what its author meant — **which is exactly why it is not a side effect to take on their behalf.** Rewriting authored data is a decision, not a repair. The dev pinned both directions.

## Scope held

`#6296` not implemented and not partially implemented — and the dev noted the repair **makes it easier**: `REFERENCE_ROOTS` is now the single place the builder states which prefixes read as references, which is precisely the seam a caller-supplied vocabulary would replace. `flow-ref-check`, the server-side validator and `packages/spec` untouched, as required. `content/docs/releases/` clean; changeset present; 3 files, +222/−2.

## Instrument discipline

- Ghost-assertion guard, both legs, on the **real component in jsdom** reading what `onCommit` emits — not `fmtValue` in isolation, per the order. RED: 4 failed / 4 passed, reproducing the card's exact `previous == 'previous.status'`. GREEN: 8 passed.
- ⭐ The four that pass on **both** legs are the controls, and the report says so explicitly — *"which is what makes them controls and what makes the reading attributable to the input rather than to a constant."*
- Stale-dist false red (20+ `TS2307`) correctly identified as a build-order artifact, **not** reported as a gate failure.
- `eslint .` over the whole `@object-ui/app-shell` package — the CI unit, so **no narrowing to declare**. The single warning on the file is pre-existing and unchanged on `origin/main`.
- Fixture sweep across `packages/` and `apps/` for any fixture pinning a quoted reference-shaped literal: **zero hits** outside the new test — i.e. the change breaks no existing authored data.

⛔ **Not enqueued yet** — CI at time of writing is 17 ✅ / 3 skip / 0 ❌ with **7 pending**. `in_progress` is not a verdict. ⛔ The `behind` reading is not being synced; thirteen PRs resolved it unaided this round.
